intervals.label: construction
intervals.note: No source consulted (checked 2026-09-17) gives an explicit end date for construction; the commissioning/dedication interval below covers the period immediately before first collisions.
intervals.quote: Brookhaven received funding to proceed with the construction of RHIC in 1991 and physics operations began in 2000.

intervals.label: commissioning and dedication
intervals.note: No source consulted (checked 2026-09-17) states the commissioning start date; the dedication (marking the end of successful commissioning) was 1999-10-04.
intervals.quote: On Monday, Oct. 4, 1999, the RHIC was dedicated following successful commissioning.

intervals.label: first collisions / physics operations begin
intervals.note: The first run (2000) collided gold ions at 65 GeV per nucleon per beam (130 GeV per nucleon pair); the interval carries those energies as its own era values.
intervals.quote: On the evening of Monday, June 12, 2000, operators in the main control room of RHIC anxiously watched control displays as the beams circulating in the collider's twin rings appeared to be colliding.

beam_energy.note: Maximum energy per nucleon of the first run; 2 x 65 GeV is the 130 GeV centre-of-mass energy above.
beam_energy.quote: In its first run, RHIC collided ions at a maximum energy of 65 billion electron volts (GeV) per nucleon (proton or neutron). The new collisions, at 100 GeV per nucleon, will deposit more energy into the collisions, raising the temperature higher.

cms_energy.display: 130 GeV per colliding nucleon pair (Au+Au, Run 1)
cms_energy.locator: abstracts of arXiv:nucl-ex/0106001 (PHENIX) and arXiv:hep-ex/0105043 (PHOBOS: 56 GeV and 130 GeV)
cms_energy.note: Run 1 (2000). PHOBOS gives two energies in the first running period, 56 and 130 GeV; 130 GeV is the highest.
cms_energy.quote: Results from the PHENIX experiment for the first RHIC run with Au-Au collisions at a nucleon-nucleon center-of-mass energy of 130 GeV are presented.

intervals.label: full design energy reached (100 GeV/nucleon, Au+Au)
intervals.note: Marks the first announced run at RHIC's full per-nucleon design energy for gold-gold collisions.
intervals.quote: The new collisions, at 100 GeV per nucleon, will deposit more energy into the collisions, raising the temperature higher.

beam_energy.quote: The new collisions, at 100 GeV per nucleon, will deposit more energy into the collisions, raising the temperature higher.

cms_energy.display: 200 GeV per colliding nucleon pair (Au+Au, Run 2)
cms_energy.locator: abstract of arXiv:nucl-ex/0209015 (PHENIX, Run II); BNL newsroom, 18 July 2001 (100 GeV per nucleon)
cms_energy.note: Run 2 (2001 to 2002): 2 x 100 GeV per nucleon.
cms_energy.quote: We show first results on phi -> K+K-, e+e-, low and intermediate mass dielectron continuum, single electrons from charm, and J/psi yields in proton-proton and Au-Au collisions at sqrt{s_{NN}}=200 GeV.

intervals.label: Run 22: highest polarized proton-proton collision energy
intervals.note: Start date is this BNL press release's own dateline (2021-12-13), announcing the start of Run 22; not the exact day polarized-proton physics collisions began within that run.
intervals.quote: This year's run will take place at the highest collision energy: 500 billion electron volts (GeV) per colliding proton pair.

cms_energy.display: 500 GeV per colliding polarized proton pair
cms_energy.note: Some RHIC spin-physics literature refers to a maximum of up to 510 GeV for polarized p+p; this was not confirmed against an official BNL quote. The official BNL press material consulted (checked 2026-09-17) states 500 GeV as 'the highest collision energy' reached, so 500 GeV is recorded rather than 510 GeV.
cms_energy.quote: This year's run will take place at the highest collision energy: 500 billion electron volts (GeV) per colliding proton pair.

intervals.label: final run and end of RHIC operations
intervals.note: RHIC's 25th and final run ended 2026-02-06; because this terminal interval has already started, the accelerator's status is 'completed'. DOE and BNL are converting the machine into the Electron-Ion Collider, reusing the tunnel, one ion storage ring, the pre-accelerator chain and "a large detector hall" (src:bnl-newsroom-eic-transformation-2026, dated 2026-04-13). The Atlas has no accelerator record for the Electron-Ion Collider yet. The BNL article says the interaction region currently occupied by STAR becomes the site of the ePIC detector, sPHENIX will be disassembled apart from its outer hadronic calorimeter (reused in ePIC), and "The removal process is expected to take place over a period of six years" (removal of about 6,500 major RHIC components began 13 April 2026).
intervals.quote: Just after 9 a.m. on Friday, Feb. 6, 2026, final beams of oxygen ions ... circulated through the twin 2.4-mile-circumference rings ... and crashed into one another at nearly the speed of light.

name: Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider
notes: site_id is set to site:bnl-upton-campus (the general BNL campus) rather than either IP-specific site, because RHIC is a ring machine spanning both interaction points and the tunnel between them, not a single point; the campus site is the most representative single location, matching the accelerator's own facility-level coordinate anchor.

Injector chain: Linac (accelerator:bnl-linac, 200 MeV) to Booster (accelerator:bnl-booster, 1.5 GeV) to AGS (accelerator:ags, 24 GeV protons) to RHIC; heavy ions entered the Booster from EBIS and, before that, from the Tandem Van de Graaffs, neither of which has a record.

Eras (2026-10-26, follow-ups 2): Run 1 (2000) at 130 GeV per nucleon pair (65 GeV per nucleon), Run 2 (from July 2001) at 200 GeV (100 GeV per nucleon), then the Run 22 proton-proton energy of 500 GeV. The headline 200 GeV is now a dated value, not drawn at 2000.

beam_energy.display: up to 250 GeV (protons); 100 GeV per nucleon (gold)
beam_energy.locator: DOE Office of Science, RHIC user-facility page, "Description"
beam_energy.note: Design top energies per beam; the highest proton energy actually used was about 255 GeV (Run 22, 510 GeV centre of mass, see the Run 22 interval).
beam_energy.quote: RHIC collides all ion beam species from protons to Uranium at energies up to 100 GeV (Giga Electron Volts) per nucleon (250 GeV for protons).

circumference.note: Derived by unit conversion: both sources state the ring size in miles only ("2.4 miles in circumference"), and 2.4 mi x 1.609344 km/mi = 3.86 km. The source figure is rounded to two significant digits, so the kilometre value is approximate, not an independent measurement.
circumference.quote: scientists, engineers, and technicians began building two separate accelerator rings, each 2.4 miles in circumference

cms_energy.display: 200 GeV per colliding gold-gold nucleon pair (design/typical top energy)
cms_energy.note: This is RHIC's top heavy-ion (Au+Au) centre-of-mass energy per colliding nucleon pair, consistent with the independently sourced per-beam figure of 100 GeV/nucleon (src:bnl-newsroom-full-energy-2001, dated 2001-07-18). RHIC also ran heavy-ion beam-energy-scan collisions down to a few GeV per nucleon pair; those lower energies are not itemised here.
cms_energy.quote: 200 billion electron volts, or GeV, per colliding pair of nuclei

injection_energy.locator: Aidala et al., Rev. Mod. Phys. 85, 655 (arXiv:1209.2803), §II.A
injection_energy.note: Injected from the AGS through the AtR line. Gold: "The nominal momentum and kinetic energy at extraction are 9.75 GeV/c and 8.86 GeV per nucleon (γ = 10.520)." (Ahrens et al., PAC 2001, section "AGS").
injection_energy.quote: The bunch of polarized protons is then transferred to the Alternating Gradient Synchrotron (AGS) and accelerated to 24 GeV before injection into RHIC.

summary.plain: A giant underground ring at Brookhaven National Laboratory that collided beams of gold atomic nuclei and of protons with aligned spins at nearly the speed of light, recreating conditions from just after the Big Bang. It ran from 2000 to 2026 and is now being rebuilt into a new machine, the Electron-Ion Collider.
summary.technical: Two intersecting 3.86 km (2.4 mi) superconducting storage rings at Brookhaven National Laboratory; the world's first heavy-ion collider and only polarized-proton collider, reaching 200 GeV per colliding gold-gold nucleon pair and up to 500 GeV in polarized proton-proton collisions. Operated 2000-2026 across 25 runs; its final run ended 2026-02-06, after which the machine began conversion into the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC).
